title: A night in Ramadan
hookLine: at forty, in Ramadan, the angel comes (97:1; 2:185)

lines: A MONTH AND A NAME, NO DATE.
cards: One night on that mountain is different from all the others he spent there. The Qur'an doesn't give its date. It gives its month, and its name, and says it is better than a thousand months.

The Prophet told his companions to look for it near the end of Ramadan, and the looking goes on: people stay awake through those last nights, praying and reading, not sure which night it is. Today: a night in Ramadan.

teach.b: Start with the month. The Qur'an names it in surah two. Pickthall's translation: "The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind."
That's why the fast is in Ramadan: it's the month the book arrived. Then the night. A short surah, the ninety-seventh, opens: "Lo! We revealed it on the Night of Power."
And it says: "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months."
The angels and the Spirit come down that night, it says, and it is peace until dawn.
A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was forty when revelation began: a man of forty, in a cave in the dark, on a night that would get its own surah. What exactly came down?

Scholars answer in more than one way. Some, following a report from Ibn 'Abbas, say the whole Qur'an was sent down that night to the nearest heaven, then revealed to the Prophet piece by piece over the years.
Others focus on this night as the beginning, when the first verses came to him in the cave. Either way, the text is clear about the night and silent about its date.

teach.h: SEEK IT IN THE ODD NIGHTS.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, he tells his companions to seek it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan.
In Muslim teaching the Night of Power comes round again every Ramadan, and so the night it came is sought each year.

how: Muslims seek Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights of Ramadan, especially the odd ones, staying up in prayer, recitation and supplication, and some spend those nights in i'tikaf in the mosque.

games.why: in Sahih al-Bukhari he says to seek it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan. the hidden date turns one night into a search.

practice: Sit for a moment as if it were the hour before dawn: the house asleep, the dark outside, nothing asking anything of you.
If you pray, there is a night prayer called tahajjud, and even two short units of it are a way to keep this hour; if you don't, just keep the quiet company a while.

wordCard.voice: Ramadan, the month the Qur'an itself names as when it was revealed, home to the hidden Night of Power, better than a thousand months. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Night of Power, or the Night of Decree, the name surah 97 gives it.

carryVoice: Your line: the night it came. Its date is hidden, so the looking goes on. Day seven hundred twenty-three, done.
